title: When the Alibi Breaks
premise: When retired detective Oscar Ishikawa finds the coffin of town founder Edmund Voss empty during a civic exhumation, she is pulled back into the work she swore off, aided by her ragtag bookshop regulars who become an unlikely investigative family. The trail leads to a double-entry ledger disguised as a rare poetry collection sold decades ago, revealing that Voss faked his death to escape prosecution for embezzling the town's trust—and that someone alive today has been killing to keep it buried. As Oscar decodes the ledger, she realizes her own missing memories of the night Voss 'died' hold the final key, and that the killer is the one person who has been quietly protecting her all along. In the end, Oscar chooses truth over the comfortable lie, exposes the conspiracy at the founders' gala, and finally lets her found family see the woman behind the alibi of ordinariness.
about_author: Gideon Yarrow is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent years cataloguing obituaries and land records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about quiet places where the past refuses to stay filed.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: Oscar Ishikawa watches from her failing bookshop's window as the town exhumed founder Edmund Voss for a centennial ceremony—only for the coffin to come up empty. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in dry humor; her carefully invisible life cracks open in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: Regulars and Suspects
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews the eccentric bookshop regulars—teen runaway Priya, insomniac accountant Marsh, and retired librarian Dot—who each remember something odd about the night Voss died. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth; she resents needing people but notices how well they fit together.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young detective Oscar worked the original 1985 death case and closed it in three days. Present-day Oscar rereads her own file and finds a page missing—one only she could have removed. POV: Oscar (with embedded past-tense sections). Emotional beat: unease at her own erased memory.

chapters.title: The Poetry Section
chapters.summary: Dot recognizes the ledger clue: Voss's rare first-edition poetry collection, donated to the library, contains marginalia in two hands. One hand is Voss's; the other is unknown. POV: Dot. Emotional beat: the thrill of an outsider contributing real value to the investigation.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Oscar discovers the marginalia numbers map to a double-entry ledger tracking money funneled from the town trust into shell accounts—still active. Someone is drawing on it now. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: cold clarity; this is no historical curiosity but a living crime.

chapters.title: The Trustee
chapters.summary: Current town matriarch Vivian Ashford, Voss's protégée, stonewalls Oscar with charm and veiled threats, reminding her how easily a bookshop lease can vanish. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: anger and recognition—power wears a friendly face here.

chapters.title: Priya's Night Shift
chapters.summary: Priya, sleeping in the shop's stockroom, witnesses someone breaking in to search Oscar's office. She photographs them but loses the shot; only a distinctive cufflink remains. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: fear transformed into belonging—she finally has something worth defending.

chapters.title: What Marsh Counted
chapters.summary: Marsh traces the shell companies and finds payments routed through the accounting firm he worked for before his breakdown—the case that broke him. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: shame curdling into resolve as his old competence returns.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Oscar confronts her own gap: the missing file page corresponds to the exact hour of Voss's death, which she cannot remember despite being first on scene. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: vertigo; the detective becomes the unreliable witness.

chapters.title: A Body in the Archive
chapters.summary: The town archivist who first flagged the empty coffin is found dead, staged as a fall. The death certificate is signed by the same doctor who certified Voss's. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief hardening into guilt—she was too slow.

chapters.title: Cufflinks and Old Money
chapters.summary: The cufflink matches a set owned by Sheriff Dane Kowalczyk, whose family fortune predates the town charter. He denies everything, convincingly—but too quickly. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: disillusionment; the badge she trusted looks like armor for the guilty.

chapters.title: Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Marsh finds a second ledger layer: disbursements labeled 'maintenance' paid annually for forty years—to someone keeping the secret. The amounts match a modest pension. Someone alive has been paid to stay silent. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: dawning horror that the conspiracy is mundane and patient.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Confession
chapters.summary: Oscar corners the elderly doctor, who admits certifying an empty coffin under pressure but swears he never saw Voss die—he was told the body was 'handled.' He names the person who told him: Oscar herself, forty years ago. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: betrayal by her own past self.

chapters.title: Alibi
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the night, Oscar realizes her unshakeable alibi—that she was seen at the diner until midnight—was manufactured. Someone fed her drinks and walked her home. Her perfect record was built on a hole she didn't know existed. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: identity collapse; the thing she prided herself on was a gift from an enemy.

chapters.title: Fire at the Shop
chapters.summary: Arson guts the bookshop's back room—the poetry section survives because Dot had borrowed it. Priya is nearly trapped inside. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: terror and fury; the found family realizes they are targets, not bystanders.

chapters.title: Vivian's Version
chapters.summary: Vivian privately offers Oscar a deal: close the case as grave robbery, take a generous stipend, restore the shop. She reveals Voss stole from the town first—or so she claims. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: temptation rendered honestly; the corrupt bargain sounds almost kind.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: Graphological comparison shows the second marginalia hand belongs to someone still writing: recent library sign-in cards. The silent pensioner has been maintaining the ledger's cover story for decades—inside the library itself. POV: Dot. Emotional beat: quiet triumph shadowed by heartbreak at the name she recognizes.

chapters.title: Marta
chapters.summary: The second hand is Marta Voss, Edmund's widow, presumed to have left town in 1986. Dot has been exchanging letters with her for years under a pen-pal alias—unwittingly helping maintain the fiction. POV: Dot. Emotional beat: devastation and loyalty in conflict; friendship versus truth.

chapters.title: The Empty Grave Digs Back
chapters.summary: Oscar confronts Marta, who confesses: Edmund faked his death to flee prosecution, and Marta stayed to draw the 'maintenance' payments and keep his legend intact—for the town's sake, she insists. But Marta didn't kill the archivist. Someone else is tying loose ends. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: pity without absolution; the mystery deepens even as it resolves.

chapters.title: The Protector
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the maintenance ledger with the sheriff's finances, Oscar identifies the killer: Sheriff Kowalczyk's father arranged the original escape, and Dane has been eliminating anyone who might reopen it—including trying to frame Oscar via her missing memories, which he induced with drugged drinks that night. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: cold rage; the man who 'protected' her was her jailer.

chapters.title: Founders' Gala
chapters.summary: At the centennial gala, Oscar stages a public reading of the decoded ledger before the whole town, with Marsh confirming figures and Priya livestreaming to prevent suppression. Dane draws a weapon; Dot's recorded confession from Marta plays over the speakers. He is arrested as Vivian's complicity unravels. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: catharsis; the invisible woman makes herself unmistakably seen.

chapters.title: Shelf Life
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the shop reopens, rebuilt by the regulars' hands, the poetry section restored to its rightful place. Oscar files her completed report on both cases—1985 and now—and sleeps without dreams for the first time in years. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: earned peace; memory recovered, family chosen, power answered.
